sentences: The game is set in the fictional asylum, a facility on an island off the coast of the city that houses criminally insane supervillains.
The game features a large ensemble of characters from the history of the hero's comics.
Three voice actors who worked on an animated series of film and television reprised their roles for the game.

A voice actor voices the hero—a superhero trained to the peak of human physical perfection and an expert in martial arts, a second voice actor voices the hero's psychopathic nemesis, the villain, and the villain's sidekick is voiced by a third.
The hero is aided by his allies, a helper (a voice actor)—who remotely provides him with intelligence, and the police commissioner (a voice actor).

In the asylum, the hero is faced with several supervillains; he must defend himself from an enraged strongman (a voice actor), subdue an indiscriminate serial killer (a voice actor), confront a monstrous inmate (a voice actor), defeat the plant-controller (a voice actor), and battle his way through hallucinogen-induced nightmares created by the toxin-maker (a voice actor).
Another villain (a voice actor) does not physically appear in the game, but communicates with the hero and challenges him to solve riddles placed around the island.

Other characters appearing in the game include the asylum's warden (also voiced by the commissioner's actor), the hero's father and mother (voiced by the hero's actor and the plant-controller's actor respectively), and an asylum guard (a voice actor).
A shape-shifting character appears in cameo, taking on the guise of other characters as he tries to trick the player into releasing him.
Another character was almost included in the game, but the developers removed him.
The body of another character is in the asylum's morgue and a ventriloquist's dummy appears several times throughout the story.
Several other characters—including five others and the asylum's founder—are referenced in the game, but do not appear in it.
After the villain assaults the city hall, he is caught by the hero and taken to the asylum, which temporarily houses many members of the villain's gang, who were transferred after a fire at a prison.
Believing the villain allowed himself to be captured, the hero accompanies him into the asylum.
The villain's plan is revealed as his sidekick takes over the security and the villain escapes into the facility, aided by a corrupt guard who kidnaps the commissioner.
The villain threatens to detonate bombs hidden around the city if anyone tries to enter the asylum, forcing the hero to work alone.
Tracking the sidekick to the medical facility to rescue the commissioner, the hero is exposed to the toxin-maker's fear toxin.
After fighting off the toxin-maker's hallucinations, the hero finds and subdues the sidekick before rescuing the commissioner.
The villain then directs the hero to the captured strongman, who has been experimented on by the asylum doctor.
The villain frees the strongman to fight the hero, who defeats him by ramming him into the ocean with his car, during which the sidekick escapes.
Afterward, he goes to a secret base installation he had hidden on the island, where he restocks his gadgets.

There, the hero learns that the villain returned to the asylum to gain access to the doctor, who has been developing a drug—a more powerful version of another drug that gives the strongman his strength—intending to use it to help patients survive more strenuous therapies.

The doctor learned that the villain had been secretly funding her research to create an army of indestructible and savage superhuman monsters; her refusal to hand over the formula precipitated the villain's return to the asylum.
While searching for the doctor, the hero destroys her drug formula before rescuing her from the serial killer.
A bomb kills the doctor, and the villain steals the completed batches of the drug.
At the penitentiary, the sidekick releases the plant-controller from her cell before being imprisoned by the hero.
The sidekick accidentally reveals that the villain has a drug production facility in the asylum's botanical gardens.
The hero travels there and learns that the drug is created by genetically modified plants.
He learns from the plant-controller that the spores required to create an antidote are found exclusively in the monstrous inmate's lair in a sewer.
Afterward, the villain injects the plant-controller with the drug, enhancing her powers, and she begins to ravage the island with giant mutant plants.
En route to the monstrous inmate, the hero reencounters the toxin-maker and pursues him into the sewers.
The toxin-maker is attacked by the monstrous inmate and dragged underwater.
The hero recovers the necessary spores and subdues the monstrous inmate before returning to the hidden base.
However, he can only synthesize one dose of the antidote before the plant-controller's plants breach the cave and destroy his equipment.
The hero returns to the botanical gardens and defeats the plant-controller, halting the rampaging plants.
The villain announces that the preparations for his party are finally complete, and the hero travels to the asylum's visitor center to confront him.
The villain reveals he has recaptured the commissioner and tries to shoot him with a drug-filled dart; the hero leaps to the commissioner's defense and is shot instead.
The hero attempts to resist the change, and an upset villain takes an overdose of the drug, mutating into a monster.
In a makeshift arena on the building's roof, the villain challenges the hero to a fight against drug-induced monsters in front of news helicopters.
The hero refuses to transform, uses the antidote on himself, and defeats the drug-affected villain and his henchmen.
The mastermind hires the villain as a distraction so that the mastermind could destroy a continent's financial districts.
He realizes his mistake when he is unable to control the villain, who captures the partner, the second sidekick and the hero's partner.
In a city, the villain brutally assaults and tortures the partner in an abandoned warehouse with a crowbar.
The villain eventually leaves and locks the partner inside the warehouse with a bomb, which explodes and kills the partner before the hero arrives.
Five years later in the city, a mysterious vigilante assembles a meeting of the city's most prominent drug dealers.

He announces a takeover of their drug trade, taking 40 percent of their profit while offering them protection from the crime boss and the hero, but threatens to kill them if anyone is caught dealing drugs to children.
The hero stops an attempted theft of a shipment that belonged to the crime boss, which contains an advanced android.
The hero destroys the android with the help of the partner's predecessor, using a new name, and discovers the thieves are working for the vigilante.
The thieves are killed by a sniper shot before they can reveal any more.
The hero identifies the shooter as the vigilante, and chases him to a chemical plant.
The vigilante references the creation of the villain in this same building before blowing up the facility.
The hero and the predecessor interrogate the villain at the asylum about the vigilante, but he denies any involvement.
An infuriated crime boss puts a hit on the vigilante for the android's destruction.
The hero and the predecessor prevent the vigilante from hijacking the crime boss's next weapon shipment.
They chase the vigilante to a train station, where he escapes after detonating a bomb, which injures the predecessor.
As the butler tends to the predecessor, the hero realizes that the vigilante is trained and has knowledge of the hero's tactics, gear and his secret identity.
The hero recalls the partner performing the same maneuvers as the sidekick and that the partner grew more violent as he aged.
The crime boss sends a team of four to lure the vigilante.
They nearly overpower him until the hero helps incapacitate three of them and the vigilante kills the fourth, horrifying the hero.
The vigilante explains that he is doing what the hero will not: killing criminals who are not afraid.
The hero analyzes a blood sample of the vigilante drawn from the battle and it matches to the partner.
After discovering that the partner's corpse is fake, the hero confronts the mastermind and demands to know the truth.

The mastermind explains that he felt responsible for the partner's death and, as a peace offering, swapped the partner's body for a fake and revived him in a pit, but following his resurrection, the partner was driven insane and escaped.
After surviving an assassination attempt by the vigilante, the crime boss sets the villain free, tasking him with killing the vigilante.
However, the villain instead abducts the crime boss and the drug dealers and plans to set them on fire.
The vigilante appears and reveals his real target is the villain.
The hero saves the hostages and the vigilante takes the villain.
The vigilante brutally beats the villain in revenge and confronts the hero.
The hero and the vigilante fight and the vigilante reveals himself as the partner.
Their fight makes its way to the dilapidated building, where the partner is keeping the villain and ends with the partner holding the hero at gunpoint.
Though having forgiven the hero for not saving him, the partner is upset and angry that the villain is still alive after killing him.
The hero admits that he considers killing the villain every time he defeats him but will not, fearing he will never be able to stop if he kills even once.
The partner tosses the hero a gun and gives him an ultimatum – he will execute the villain unless the hero shoots him.
The hero refuses and drops the gun, causing the partner to shoot at the hero.
The hero dodges the bullet, throws a projectile, which jams and destroys the partner's pistol.
The partner sets off a time bomb and the hero subdues the villain before attempting to save the partner.
The bomb explodes; the hero and the villain survive, but the partner is gone.
The villain is returned to the asylum and the crime boss is arrested.
At the hidden base, the butler offers to remove the glass case display of the partner's sidekick costume, but the hero refuses, claiming it does not change anything.
A final flashback shows the partner's first day as the sidekick, which he cheerfully declares is the best day of his life.
The game features a large ensemble cast of characters from the history of the hero's comics.

Returning characters from the previous game include the hero (a voice actor), the villain (a voice actor)—in what the actor stated would be his final time voicing the character; (he subsequently reprised the role in the game's successor)—the warden-turned-mayor (a voice actor), the police commissioner (a voice actor), and a reporter (a voice actor).
Returning villains include four others, each with their voice actor.
The villain's sidekick also returns, voiced by a new voice actor, who replaces the previous one.

The hero's supporting cast introduces an ally (a voice actor), a partner (a voice actor), and the hero's butler (a voice actor), who provides radio support alongside the returning helper (a voice actor).
Another ally appears as a playable character outside of the main story via challenge maps.

Other characters marking their debut in the series include the manipulative warden of the prison (a voice actor), another villain (also voiced by the partner's actor), and a rival villain (a voice actor).
An actress lends her voice as the assassin leader's daughter, and another voice actor voices both the scientist and another villain.
Other characters include the zombie (also voiced by a returning actor), the shapeshifter (a voice

actor), the assassin leader (a voice actor), the mind-controlling villain (a voice actor), and another assassin (a voice actor), who has infiltrated the prison to kill several high-profile character targets.
Another villain (also voiced by the hero's actor), a mysterious figure (a voice actor), and another reporter (also voiced by the ally's actor) also appear.
One more villain (also voiced by the rival villain's actor), yet another villain (a voice actor), and the scientist's wife make cameo appearances in the game.
The events of the game are set 18 months after the previous game.
The asylum's erstwhile director has taken credit for halting the villain's armed siege, using this distinction to become mayor of the city.

Declaring both the asylum and the penitentiary no longer suitable to contain the city's detainees, the mayor's administration orders both facilities closed, and he purchases the city's most notorious slums and turns them into an immense prison enclosure.
This facility is subsequently placed in the care of a psychiatrist—who is secretly manipulating the mayor—and monitored by a rogue private military firm.
The psychiatrist permits the inmates to do as they please, so long as they do not attempt to escape.
A wary hero maintains his own vigil over the new project, afraid that the chaotic situation there will get out of hand.
Meanwhile, the villain is dying from a disease caused by his previous overdose of the formula, an unstable steroid mutagen that turns men into powerful and savage monsters.
At a press conference held by the hero's civilian alter ego to declare his opposition to the prison, the firm's mercenaries arrest and imprison him in the prison itself.
The psychiatrist discloses his knowledge of the alter ego's dual identity as the hero before releasing him into the prison's criminal populace.
While the psychiatrist prepares to commence the protocol, the alter ego obtains his equipment via airdrop from the butler, allowing him to become the hero.
He first saves the ally from being executed by another villain, who hopes to gain respect by murdering her.
After the villain attempts to assassinate the ally, the hero tracks him to his hideout in a steel mill, believing the villain may know the truth behind the protocol.
There, the hero learns that the unstable properties of the formula are mutating in the villain's blood, gradually killing him.
The villain captures the hero and performs a blood transfusion on him, infecting him with the same fatal disease.
The villain also reveals that the city's hospitals have been poisoned with his infected blood.
Desperate to save himself and innocent citizens, the hero seeks out the scientist, who has been developing a cure but has since been kidnapped by the rival villain.
Tracking the rival villain to his fortified museum, the hero defeats his forces, his imprisoned monster, the zombie, and ultimately the rival villain himself, before liberating the scientist.
The scientist tells the hero that he has created a cure, but it is rendered useless via instability.

The hero deduces that the therapeutic properties of the assassin leader's blood can complete the cure and tracks one of his assassins to his underground lair, leading the hero into a confrontation with the assassin leader and his daughter, the hero's former lover.
With the assassin leader's blood, the scientist is able to develop an antidote, but the villain's sidekick steals it before the hero can use it.
When the hero returns to the villain, he finds the latter's health has been restored.
During a fight between the two, the psychiatrist activates the protocol, which is revealed to be a scheme to wipe out the entire population of the prison and destroy the criminal element of the city.
The firm's troops begin executing inmates as the psychiatrist launches missile strikes on the prison's denizens from his base in a tower.
A missile hits the steel mill, burying the hero under rubble.
Before the villain can take advantage of the situation, the daughter arrives and offers him immortality in exchange for sparing the hero's life.
After escaping with the help of the ally, the hero is convinced by the butler to end the protocol before pursuing the daughter and the villain.
The hero infiltrates the tower and disables the protocol.
The assassin leader is revealed to be the true mastermind behind the prison and mortally wounds the psychiatrist for failing to defeat the hero.
The villain, a former member of an organization, leads an attack on an intelligence-agency plane over a foreign country to abduct a nuclear physicist.

Meanwhile, eight years after the death of the city's district attorney and the arrest of another villain, organized crime has been eradicated in the city by an act, legislation that gives expanded powers to the police.
The police commissioner has kept the district attorney's killing spree a secret and allowed the blame for his crimes to fall on the vigilante.
The billionaire, still mourning the death of a woman, has become a recluse.
The villain conspires to help a board member of the company take over the company.
A cat burglar steals the billionaire's fingerprints from his mansion for the board member, but he double-crosses her, and she alerts the police.
The villain's henchmen capture the commissioner in the sewers but he escapes and is found by a steadfast police officer of the city, an orphan who has deduced the billionaire's secret identity.
The officer persuades the billionaire to resume his vigilantism.
The villain attacks the stock exchange and uses the billionaire's fingerprints to verify fraudulent transactions, leaving the billionaire ousted from his company and bankrupt.

Fearing the billionaire will purposely get himself killed fighting the villain, his butler reveals to him that the woman was going to marry the district attorney, and thus, the billionaire should let her go.
When the billionaire does not give up, the butler resigns and leaves the mansion.
The vigilante encounters the cat burglar, and both narrowly escape the villain's henchmen.
The villain kills the board member to pursue his own goals while the billionaire and the company's new CEO become lovers.
The cat burglar agrees to take the vigilante to the villain, but instead leads him into a trap under a tower.
The villain, aware of the vigilante's identity, gloats that he intends to fulfill the mastermind's mission to destroy the city before brutally crippling the vigilante in combat.
He takes the billionaire to an ancient underground prison abroad, where the billionaire learns that the mastermind's wife was sent there while pregnant with his child.
The child was born and raised there, but had a protector who helped them escape.
Back in the city, the villain detonates explosives, trapping the police forces in the sewers, destroying all but one bridge surrounding the city, and killing the city's mayor.
He forces the physicist to convert the fusion reactor core owned by the company into a decaying neutron bomb before publicly executing him.
Effectively taking over the city, he exposes the district attorney's crimes to the world, and releases the prisoners of the penitentiary.
The villain also has the city's elite exiled and killed in proletarian kangaroo courts presided over by a man.
Five months later, the billionaire, now healed, escapes the prison.
As the vigilante, he returns to the city and frees the police to battle the villain's army together.
During the battle, the CEO stabs the vigilante, revealing herself as the mastermind's daughter.
The villain is her decoy and guardian who had helped her escape the pit, becoming mauled in the process.
The daughter activates the bomb, but it fails due to the commissioner blocking the signal.
The cat burglar kills the villain and helps the vigilante pursue the daughter, hoping to return the bomb to the reactor chamber, where it can be stabilized.
The daughter's truck crashes, but she remotely floods and destroys the reactor chamber before dying.
With no way to stop the detonation, the vigilante reveals his identity to the commissioner, and uses his aerial craft to haul the bomb over the bay, where it safely explodes.
In the aftermath, the vigilante is presumed dead and honored as a hero.
Since the billionaire is also presumed dead, his mansion becomes an orphanage, and the billionaire's estate is left to the butler.

The commissioner finds the signal light repaired, while an ally discovers that the billionaire had fixed the aircraft's malfunctioning autopilot, implying that he escaped the aircraft before the detonation.
In a foreign city, drinking a liqueur, the butler discovers that the billionaire is alive and in a relationship with the cat burglar, and they acknowledge each other with a smile.
A disillusioned officer, whose legal first name is revealed, resigns from the police department, and receives a package leading him to the hidden base.
The protagonist is the eight-year-old son of a doctor, a mayoral candidate for the city, and his wife.
After receiving death threats, the father contacts his friend from his military service to become the head of security at the mansion.
During an outing with his parents, the protagonist is taken hostage by a mugger.
He demands that the parents pay a ransom for the return of their son and attempts to remove the mother's pearl necklace.
The father tries to intervene and the criminal shoots them both in front of the protagonist.
Following the protagonist's return to the mansion, the friend learns that he has been named as the protagonist's legal guardian by the parents in the event of their absence.
The friend reluctantly agrees and presents himself to the protagonist as his butler.
As a teenager, the protagonist befriends his classmate and develops a rivalry with her twin brother.
He also learns about his mother's family manor, where she lived as a child; her mother suffered a mental breakdown when she was 12 years old, murdering her husband and then committing suicide.
The family manor is believed to be cursed due to the actions of the mother's mother, causing all members of the mother's bloodline to become insane.
The protagonist convinces the butler to train him in various forms of martial arts and acrobatics, and also learns investigative techniques.
Following this training, he discovers evidence that the mayor was involved in his parents' assassination.
Years later, the protagonist's investigation leads him to a police detective who was the first to arrive at the parents' murder scene and later left the police to work in the mayor's office.
The protagonist dons a bat-themed costume as a disguise to frighten his parents' alleged killers.
He attacks the ex-detective, but the grapple gun he developed malfunctions and the ex-detective escapes.

The protagonist then seeks the help of a 22-year-old intern at a medical company, who agrees to repair his equipment in exchange for funding for a project to develop artificial limbs for amputees, which the intern wants to use to give his five-year-old niece a new arm.

Meanwhile, a detective of the city's police department meets his new partner, an experienced detective from another city's police who has come to the city to solve the parents' murders and revive his fading career.

Following an altercation between the protagonist and the mayor's bodyguards at a function organized by the mayor, the protagonist's alter ego is given a name by the press and becomes a public sensation.
The mayor, infuriated by the vigilante's actions, orders one of his henchmen, a serial killer, to kill the ex-detective.
The vigilante's investigation takes him to the family manor, where the serial killer had been placing his victims.
A chain of events leads to the kidnapping of the detective's 17-year-old daughter by a petty thug working for the mayor.

The detective learns that the partner is indirectly responsible for the kidnapping, since he checked out the parents' murder files under the detective's name, and the detective was threatened by the mayor to stay out of the archives to keep him from discovering his complicity in the murders.

The detective, angry, but also terrified about what the partner did, explains to him that he was once as fearless and resistant to the city's corruption as the partner, but became afraid and compliant and lets criminals do their business so that he can protect the daughter from their wrath following his wife's death in an automobile accident, which he believes was arranged by the city's corrupt elite.
An apologetic partner helps the detective find the thug, who is violently forced to reveal the daughter's location.
While she struggles against the serial killer, the vigilante, the detective and the partner unite in the search for her.
The vigilante eventually intercepts the serial killer while the detective rescues the daughter; the vigilante overpowers the serial killer, who is then arrested by the detective and the partner.
In a subsequent confrontation between the vigilante and the mayor, the mayor reveals his intention was for the ex-detective to murder the father, but he and his wife ran into the mugger instead.
The mayor then prepares to kill an unmasked protagonist but is fatally shot by the butler.
The thug is arrested and the serial killer, whose identity is revealed, is transferred to an institute for the criminally insane, run by a doctor, from which the serial killer originally escaped.
The daughter begins to idolize the vigilante, studying martial arts and criminology, and sketching potential costumes.
The partner, on the other hand, is traumatized by his experiences and succumbs to alcoholism.
After the mayor's crimes are posthumously outed, he is replaced by the classmate as the mayor of the city.

The intern, after seeing the vigilante uses the grapple gun he repaired for the protagonist on the news, deduces that the young billionaire is the vigilante and begins building a bat-themed arsenal for him, hoping to become a part of the action.
The protagonist is left disappointed by the truth behind his parents' death, but with the butler's encouragement, decides that he will continue on to refine his new persona as the vigilante.
The story concludes with the depiction of an enigmatic man reviewing information on the vigilante.
The events depicted in the second volume occur six months after those of the first volume.
A mysterious serial killer, who has given himself a nickname, is murdering people in the city, hoping to get the vigilante's attention.

Elsewhere, after losing track of one of the drug dealers he fought during a car chase, the protagonist has the intern (who is promoted as the head of the company's research and development department) build him a custom-made race car.

The partner remains traumatized over the travesties that occurred in the family manor, and the detective tries to help him to combat his alcoholism, as he needs the partner as an ally in order to combat corruption in the city.

The classmate comes to the mansion to visit the protagonist in the hopes that, as the CEO of the company, he could help her find five of the remaining members of the former mayor's criminal organization within the city's legislature.
The game features a large ensemble cast of characters from the history of the hero's comics.
The main character is the hero (a voice actor)—a superhero trained to the peak of human physical and mental perfection and an expert in martial arts.

He is supported by his allies, a partner (a voice actor), another ally (a voice actor), a third ally (a voice actor), a woman (a voice actor)—who assists the hero covertly as a hacker—and her father, the police commissioner (a voice actor).

The hero's loyal butler (a voice actor) and a colleague from his company (a voice actor) provide the hero with tactical support, and a holy warrior (a voice actor) aims to replace the hero as the city's protector.

Throughout the city, the hero is faced with several supervillains: he must overcome the villain's (a voice actor) plot to threaten the city, dismantle the arms dealer's (a voice actor) weapon dealing operation, put an end to the bank robber's (a voice actor) bank heists, conquer the challenger's (a voice actor) challenges, capture the plant-controller (a voice actor), and subdue an accomplice (a voice actor), who wants revenge against the hero for the death of the hero's psychopathic nemesis (a voice actor), who appears in the game as a hallucination.

The game introduces the militia leader (also voiced by the bank robber's actor), a new villain created by the studio, the comics publisher's CCO and comic-book writer, and its co-publisher and comic artist.
The militia leader is a militarized version of the hero, with the logo of the asylum facility worn as an emblem on his chest.

Other villains include a pyromaniac (a voice actor), a beastly creature (a voice actor), a veteran assassin (a voice actor), a serial killer (a voice actor), a religious fanatic (a voice actor), and an impersonator (also voiced by the hero's actor), who is impersonating the hero's civilian alter-ego.

The game also features appearances and voice cameos by various characters drawn from the history of the hero's comics and the previous games in the series, including a pharmaceutical businessman (a voice actor), two reporters (one also voiced by the third ally's actor, the other by a voice actor), a police officer (a voice actor), a corporate businessman (a voice actor), a crimefighter, another serial killer, and a mutated gangster (a voice actor), while the game's downloadable content features appearances by six further characters (each with a voice actor).
The game also makes references to many characters from the history of the hero and his comics publisher.

Nine months after the death of the nemesis during the events of the previous game, the hero is struggling to cope with the absence of his archenemy and the uncomfortable feeling that the pair shared a bond deeper than either could admit.
Without the nemesis's presence, the city's citizens have never felt safer, and crime in the city has declined significantly.
However, this gives the hero's enemies, including the arms dealer, the challenger, the bank robber, and the accomplice, a chance to unite with the singular goal of defeating the hero.
Having anticipated a new threat, the hero has continued to develop crime-fighting technology and maintain a vigil over the city.

On Halloween night, the villain, who the hero had defeated in an earlier game, threatens the city with his newly created strain of fear toxin and bombs planted throughout the city, forcing the evacuation of the city's six million civilians.
Only criminals remain in the city, leaving the commissioner and the city's police department outnumbered.
The game's city is approximately five times the scale of the open-air prison in the previous game.
The game takes place in the center of the city, which is split into three islands, with various districts such as the neon-tinged Chinese quarter, and the industrial shipping yard.

The first island features shorter buildings, disheveled areas, and abandoned docks, while the second island is a modern development of skyscrapers built on the ruins of the city's slums, and the third island is an older metropolis with a tower at its center.
The hacker has set up her communications headquarters in the city's clock tower, which also houses a makeshift hidden base.
On Halloween, the villain forces an evacuation of the city after threatening to unleash his new fear toxin.
The hero tracks the villain to a hideout where he rescues the imprisoned plant-controller, who had refused to join the hero's other rogues in the villain's plot.
The hacker identifies a chemical plant as the source of the villain's toxin.
The hero investigates the facility and discovers a large militia being dispatched to occupy the city, led by the mysterious militia leader.
The hero locates the villain, who has transformed the building into a toxic bomb meant to engulf the entire coast.
The villain reveals that he has kidnapped the hacker before escaping.
Exposing himself to the toxin, the hero inhibits the bomb's blast radius before the nemesis confronts him.
A flashback reveals that before the nemesis's death, his infected blood was used in blood transfusions, infecting five people, including the hero.
Concealing his infection, the hero imprisoned the four other patients, who were physically and mentally transforming into the nemesis.
The nemesis, existing as a mental projection produced by the infected blood and fear toxin, frequently appears to taunt the hero and twist his perception of reality.
After the hero escapes the chemical plant, he alerts the commissioner to his daughter's kidnapping, revealing that she aids his vigilantism.
The commissioner, feeling betrayed, abandons him and leaves to find the villain on his own.
The hero learns that the villain recruited a business mogul to build a mass dispersal device for the fear toxin.

Aboard the mogul's airship, the hero finds the villain, but a dose of his fear toxin allows the nemesis's persona to temporarily assume control of the hero while the militia leader extracts the device.
Recovering, the hero locates the hacker in the villain's hideout, where he watches her shoot herself after being exposed to fear toxin.
The accomplice seizes the hero's makeshift base inside a film studio to rescue the transforming patients.
The hero and the partner capture the accomplice and the infected, but one of the patients kills the others and himself, believing that the hero will become the perfect nemesis.
Realizing that the hero is infected, the partner attempts to imprison him, but is instead locked in a cell by the hero for his own safety.
The militia leader activates the device, flooding the city with fear toxin.
The hero destroys the tank carrying the device and convinces the plant-controller to empower an ancient tree that can neutralize the toxin.
In a flashback to his childhood, the billionaire flees his parents' funeral.
He falls into a cave, where a circling vortex of bats elevates him back to the surface.
In the present, eighteen months after his cataclysmic battle with a general in another city, the superhero has become a controversial figure.
He is now a billionaire who has operated in the city as a masked vigilante for twenty years.
Having witnessed the battle in person, he sees the superhero as an existential threat to humanity.
The reporter, the superhero's civilian identity, seeks to condemn the vigilante's brutal methods in newspaper articles.

A corporate mogul attempts to persuade a senator to allow him to import a green rock discovered in the aftermath of the general's terraforming attempt, so that it can be used as a deterrent against future alien threats.
She declines, but the mogul makes alternative plans with the senator's subordinate, who grants him access to the general's corpse and the alien scout ship.
The billionaire attends a gala at the mogul's company to steal the company's encrypted data, but an antiquities dealer steals it first; she returns it to the billionaire.
The billionaire dreams of a post-apocalyptic world where he leads rebels against an evil version of the superhero.
He is awakened by an unidentified person, appearing through a portal, who tells him that a woman is "the key" and urges him to find "the others" before vanishing.
The decrypted data reveals the mogul's files on several metahumans across the globe.
One is the dealer, who appears in a photo from World War I.
A widely publicized congressional hearing at the capitol, led by the senator, is held to question the superhero's actions and intentions.
A lead-covered bomb smuggled in by the mogul detonates, killing everyone present.
The superhero blames himself for not detecting it and self-imposes exile.
Believing the superhero was complicit in the attack, the vigilante breaks into the mogul's company and steals the green rock to weaponize it.
Wearing an armored exosuit and wielding a green-rock spear, he lights the signal light and awaits a battle with the superhero.
The mogul lures the superhero out by kidnapping the reporter's adoptive mother, and the woman.
The superhero saves the woman and confronts the mogul, who reveals he orchestrated the vigilante's paranoia.
He demands that the superhero kill the vigilante in exchange for the adoptive mother's life.
The superhero arrives in the city and tries reasoning with the vigilante, who attacks him using green-rock-laced gas.
They battle, but the vigilante proves victorious.
As the vigilante prepares to kill him with the spear, the superhero pleads with him to "save" his adoptive mother, calling her by name – the same name as the vigilante's mother.
The vigilante hesitates as the woman arrives and explains the superhero's pleading.
Realizing he has been manipulated, and recognizing the superhero's humanity, the vigilante rescues the adoptive mother.
The mogul, desperate to kill the superhero, executes his backup plan: unleashing a monster genetically engineered using DNA from both the general's body and his own.
A sword-wielding dealer joins the vigilante and the superhero in their fight against the creature.
The vigilante realizes its vulnerability to the green rock.
A weakened superhero fatally impales the creature with the green-rock spear, but it deals him a deadly blow in return.
The superhero passes away in the woman's arms.
Following the mogul's arrest, the vigilante confronts him in prison, where the mogul gloats that the superhero's death has made the world vulnerable to an alien threat.
A memorial is held for the superhero in the other city, while the billionaire and the dealer attend a funeral for the reporter, also declared dead.
The billionaire tells the dealer that he regrets failing the superhero and asks for her help in forming a team of metahumans to protect the planet in the superhero's absence.
As they leave, the dirt atop the reporter's coffin levitates.
Within the comic-book portion of the toy universe, the vigilante protects the city and fights crime.

During his latest mission to stop the villain and his cronies from destroying the city, the vigilante succeeds, but additionally hurts the villain's feelings when he deems him a perfunctory presence in his life, leading the villain to develop a plot for revenge.
The following day, the vigilante's alter ego attends a gala celebrating both the retirement of the commissioner and the ascension of his daughter to replace him.
While smitten by the daughter, the alter ego absent-mindedly agrees to adopt an enthusiastic orphan.
He is then infuriated by the daughter's plans to restructure the police to function without the vigilante.
The villain crashes the party with his cronies, but with the exception of one crony, they abruptly surrender to the police.
With so many villains incarcerated, the vigilante becomes despondent as the city no longer requires his crime-fighting skills.

Believing the villain is up to something, the vigilante plans to steal a superhero's projector, a device that can banish anyone to the zone, which houses some of the most dangerous villains in the toy universe, only for the butler to intervene and advise him to care for the orphan.
The vigilante initially refuses, so the butler allows the orphan to enter the hidden base.
Appearing as the vigilante before the orphan, the alter ego states that he is additionally adopting him and christens him as his sidekick.
The vigilante and the sidekick recover the projector from a chamber in the superhero's fortress, break into the asylum and successfully send the villain to the zone.
Suspecting that the villain wanted to be sent there, the daughter detains the duo.

While the projector is being seized as evidence, the crony steals it back as part of the villain's plan and frees him, allowing him to return to the city with all the villains he had recruited in the zone as they ravage the city and conquer the mansion.
Realizing that the city does need the vigilante after all, the daughter releases him and the sidekick and teams up with them and the butler to stop the new threat.
Although his teammates achieve some success in fighting the villains, the vigilante forcibly sends them away and confronts the villain alone, fearing that he might lose them just like his parents.
Believing that the vigilante is incapable of changing his ways, the villain sends him to the zone before stealing the hidden base's stash of confiscated bombs to destroy the city.
Meanwhile, the zone's prison warden shows the vigilante his constant mistreatment of those closest to him; he finally accepts his greatest fear of being part of a family and vows to better himself.
The vigilante's teammates return to the fight to help him, but are endangered themselves.

The vigilante makes a deal with the warden to temporarily return to the city to retrieve the zone's escaped villains and arrives in time to save his teammates, apologizing to them for leaving them and requesting their help to defeat the villain.
They agree, with the daughter taking on a mantle of her own.
With help from the villain's former team, the vigilante and his team defeat the escaped villains and send them back to the zone.
Unfortunately, the villain's bombs detonate, causing the plates below the city to divide in half and tear apart.
The vigilante convinces the villain to help him by telling him he gives him purpose to be the hero he is.
With the help of every civilian and villain, they manage to save the city, chain-linking themselves to reattach the plates.
The vigilante reveals to the sidekick that he is the man who adopted him, then goes to return to the zone to face the consequences of his earlier behavior.
However, the warden allows him to stay after realizing he is a hero and seeing how he changed to save everyone.
Afterward, the vigilante gives their adversaries a head start, knowing they will be no match for his team.
The vigilante and his two allies pursue the villain in a reckless high-speed chase through the city, causing significant property damage and nearly killing multiple bystanders.
The vigilante eventually corners the villain and chases him on foot into a pharmaceutical warehouse.
He beats the villain and is goaded into force-feeding him a bottle of unknown medication which turns him sane.
The vigilante's allies watch in disgust and footage of the assault is leaked to the news.
In light of these events, the city begins to debate over whether the vigilante is doing more harm than good.
The billionaire's recent violence stems from the butler being near death, kept alive only by a cryogenic technology.
The villain, now using his real name, wins a case against the police department for insufficient evidence and for non-intervention in his beating.
Freed, the sane man visits the villain's accomplice, who attacks him and insists he is not himself.
Saved by a second accomplice, the sane man learns she is the original but was replaced.
When the villain's obsession with the vigilante culminated in a victim's torture, the original accomplice left him to try and help save the victim's life.
During a subsequent bank robbery, the villain had unwittingly adopted a hostage as the new accomplice.
The billionaire and a scientist develop a treatment for their loved ones' cryogenic illnesses.
Despite not being fully tested, the scientist attempts to use the new system to resuscitate his wife.
Having anticipated this, the billionaire hooks the system up to the scientist's suit, curing him of his own illness, but aging him horribly.

Later, the billionaire is left shaken by the discovery that many of his fellow billionaires have been profiting off of the vigilante's destructive battles with criminals by purchasing destroyed properties then flipping them after they are repaired by the city, along with the revelation that his father funded the scientist's father to create the cryogenic technology, circumventing national laws by tunneling under a foreign embassy in the city.
The scientist's father later cut ties with the billionaire's father to build a superweapon.
Now running for councilman, the sane man funds construction of a library in an impoverished district and befriends an ex-police officer who runs a local youth group.
Using another villain's technology, the sane man mind controls a third villain into servitude.
He then drugs the vigilante's rogues gallery with drinks laced with the third villain's essence which he can use to control them by proxy.
Making the villains rampage across the city as a distraction, the sane man gains access to restricted documents and discovers a hidden tax fund for the vigilante's collateral damage.

In an attempt to move the villains to a less-populated area, the vigilante baits them into attacking the sane man's library in the district, thinking that they would not attack the sane man's property; the villains proceed to raze the library and damage the neighborhood.
Critically injured, the billionaire returns to the hidden base and collapses at the butler's bedside.
He wakes to find the butler has used his life-support to stabilize the billionaire at the cost of his own life.
His two allies grow increasingly concerned with the billionaire's developing obsession in convicting the sane man.
The former hostage, now the new villain, gains control of the third villain's remains, placing the city's villains under her power.
The sane man presents the police department with an offer.
The sane man offers to use his power as a councilman to reallocate the hidden tax fund to the police department, giving the city an accountable, state-sanctioned, vigilante-alternative task force.
The new villain attacks the police department, prompting the police commissioner to side with the sane man and place an APB on the vigilante.
Bested by the task force, which has recruited the ex-officer and the vigilante's two allies, the vigilante is arrested by the sane man.
The new villain uses the scientist's father's superweapon to freeze the harbor, demanding that the villain be given to her.
The sane man develops a tolerance to his medication, making him periodically revert into the villain.
The sane man frees the vigilante, asking for help stopping the new villain in exchange for a confession, provided the original accomplice's continued freedom.
The sane man, the vigilante and the task force organize an assault on the new villain's freeze ray, piloting a fleet of the vigilante's cars taken from the mansion.
Making peace with his two allies and the commissioner, the vigilante races through the city's tunnels with the sane man, who has reverted to the villain.
The task force bests the new villain's forces and reverses the freeze ray, flooding the tunnels.
Overpowering the new villain, the villain releases the third villain and undoes the mind control.

With the vigilante protecting him from the third villain, the villain and the original accomplice apprehend the new villain, and the sane man, gaining control for a last time, confesses his love for the original accomplice.

Confessing to his crimes, the sane man surrenders and is granted a nicer asylum cell and a wedding to the original accomplice; as he finishes his vows, the sane man permanently reverts to the villain.
Using the sane man's remaining funds, the original accomplice begins restoring the district.
Confronting the original accomplice, the vigilante reveals that she manufactured the villain's medication and orchestrated events so the opening chase would end in the factory and be recorded.
While battling the gorilla at the asylum, the vigilante is caught in the gorilla's time displacement machine and sent to a feudal country.
There, he is chased by ashigaru samurai soldiers working for the villain.
During his escape, the vigilante meets up with a woman, who reveals everyone else arrived two years earlier due to the vigilante being in the outermost area affected by the machine.
He learns from her that all of the city's top criminals have become feudal lords after deceiving the daimyo of the era, battling each other until only one state remains.
To stop the villains from altering history, the vigilante and the woman must get to the machine in the castle (formerly the asylum).
The vigilante discovers that the butler is also in the past and has built a hidden base outside a city.
When the villain's troops ambush the hideout, the vigilante storms his way in his car towards the castle, which transforms into a robot fortress.
As the vigilante confronts the villain, he is forced to leave and save a mother and child from being crushed by the robot's hand.
He transforms his motorcycle into an armored suit to defeat another villain and stop the robot hand, only to learn the mother is the villain's accomplice in disguise.
As the vigilante is surrounded by the villain's minions, he is whisked away by ninja led by the leader of a clan from a province.
The vigilante learns the clan helped four of his allies upon their arrival and the clan has followed a prophecy of a foreign bat ninja restoring order to the land.
One of the allies gives the vigilante an invitation from the gorilla to a nearby hot spring.
There, the gorilla explains he intended to send the villains away so he could take the city for himself, but the vigilante's interference sent them to the feudal country instead.
The vigilante and the gorilla agree to work together to return to the city.
The vigilante, the gorilla, the woman, the vigilante's family and the clan battle the villain and his forces by the river.

They defeat the villain and the accomplice, but the gorilla turns on the vigilante, revealing his alliance with another villain before the villain and the accomplice escape and blow up their own ship, taking the vigilante down with it.

Having captured a power converter from the accomplice, the woman attempts to bargain with the gorilla in bringing her back to the city; however, they need to obtain other power converters from three other villains to complete the machine.
Two days later, the vigilante recovers from his wounds and encourages his family to learn the ways of the ninja to defeat the gorilla.
Another ally locates the villain and the accomplice, but the vigilante discovers they lost their memories from the explosion and are living as farmers.
A month later, the villains mobilize their castle robots for battle at a field.
The vigilante leads his family and the clan into the battlefield.
After defeating the other villains, the gorilla controls them with the intent of ruling the country himself.
The villain and the accomplice crash his party from above, reclaiming their castle from the gorilla.
The vigilante's family saves the woman and the gorilla before the villain merges all of the castles into a super robot.
An injured gorilla gives the control of his army of monkeys to the vigilante.
The same ally enables them to merge into one giant samurai monkey, who in turn fuses with a swarm of bats to form a god.
The villain reveals to the vigilante that as farmers, he and the accomplice planted special flowers that restored their memories after blooming.
As the castle falls, the vigilante and the villain engage in a sword fight.
Using his ninjutsu skills, the vigilante defeats the villain.
With the villain and the other villains defeated, the clan begins work to restore the feudal country and the vigilante's family returns the villains to the present day.
In a mid-credits scene, the woman sells weapons and furniture from the castle robots to an antique shop, while the vigilante's alter ego rides a horse-driven car to a party hosted by the mayor.
